Pointer value `pvVar5` truncated by cast to `int` (sub-pointer width) — correct on the 32-bit matching build, a hard `cast from pointer to smaller type` error at 64-bit. If the value is used as an integer (delta, address print, hash), rewrite the cast as `uintptr_t`/`intptr_t` in a .keep.

Raw hex address 0x1c6e360 assigned to bare local `this_ptr_00`. The decompiler dropped a symbolic reference — either a data-symbol pointer (recover the symbol from the .asm and replace `this_ptr_00` with symbolic global/array indexing, §11) or a dead code-address store from return-address tracking (delete it, §14). Magic addresses do not survive the relink.

Watcom shadow-pointer walk — `pCVar11` self-updates via the address of ONE sibling scalar field whose byte offset equals the array element stride (e.g. `(T *)&pCVar11->owner`). Replace `pCVar11->some_array[0]` reads with direct indexing on the original pointer; drop the shadow init and self-update.

Ghidra pre-increment-array-walk loop artifact on `pCVar11` (per-iteration advance via struct-field/pointer arithmetic — single-var `pCVar11 = pCVar11;` self-assign, two-var `tmp = &pCVar11->field; pCVar11 = tmp;` ping-pong, or a bare `pCVar11 = pCVar11 + N;` advance followed by a `*pCVar11 =` store — plus a constant-index store on `pCVar11`). Watcom's advance-then-displaced-store (`ADD reg,N` / store `[reg + -N]`) loses the displacement here, so every store lands one element late and the first is never written. The stride/sentinel are baked from the original struct layout, so it overruns on any layout change (e.g. the 64-bit port). Always wrong as-decoded; cross-reference .asm and rewrite as a straightforward for-loop in a .keep (watch for the skip-row store-offset bug).
suspects.match: do { advance(var via &field or +N); var[K]/arr[0]... store; ...}
